what_it_does: Brain-machine interfaces implanted in the brain need to decode spoken words from raw electrical signals captured by electrodes, but doing this with a standard computer chip would drain a person's battery in minutes. This specialized processor is designed just for that one job: it runs a small neural network to turn electrical signals into phonemes (basic speech sounds), then uses a language model to guess which word was intended. The processor consumes almost no power—about as much as a hearing aid—enabling it to run implanted BMI systems for days.
